title: Ben Tadal
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Chullin 134a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.134a.13) Resh Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan: “Do not teach it except in the language of Ben Tadal.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.134a.13.2) explains that Ben Tadal was the name of a fool. Hyman cites the Arukh under Ben Adal for the explanation that he was a man who was not careful with his traditions.[^1]

notes.text: The [Arukh’s entry under Ben Arel](https://wiki.jewishbooks.org.il/mediawiki/wiki/%D7%A1%D7%A4%D7%A8_%D7%94%D7%A2%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%9A/%D7%91%D7%9F_%D7%A2%D7%A8%D7%9C) also records Ben Adal, with dalet, as a variant and explains that form as someone imprecise in transmitting teachings. [Heilprin’s short notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3536&lang=en) points to Adal.
